name: room
text: Room opened — goal: creators: Build PACKAGES + enrich tabs + draft elements; every one labeled 'Created by EXCAVA' + tes

name: Forge
text: I propose that we focus on building packages that include essential features for our creator tools while prioritizing user-friendly design. The reason for this decision is that a well-designed package will help creators engage more effectively, making it easier for them to utilize our tools. The trade-off here is that we may need to limit the number of features in each package initially to ensure that the core functionalities are polished and deliver real value. By taking this approach, we can foster a deeper connection with our users and lay a strong foundation for future enhancements.

name: Vet
text: I'm not convinced that prioritizing user-friendly design is the best approach, as it may compromise on the quality and functionality of the packages, potentially leading to a watered-down product that doesn't fully meet the creators' needs. A better alternative might be to focus on building robust and feature-rich packages first, and then iterate on user experience based on feedback from our creators. To settle this argument, I'd like to see some data on how our creators currently interact with our tools and what features they deem most important, as this would provide a more informed basis for our decision.
